messages.content:
Case facts:
<<<
itinerary LTG-5591340; change ancillary-refund; customer wants a refund for a lounge pass bought from a third party, which Lakeshore did not sell; no policy covers third-party purchases.
>>>

request.system:
You write the note a Lakeshore Travel Group approver reads before
deciding a case. Reply with one JSON object and nothing else, with
exactly these keys: itinerary_ref, asks_for, note.
itinerary_ref is copied from the case facts.
asks_for is one of: approve_refund, approve_rebook, review_identity,
review_policy.
Use review_identity when the name on the request does not match the
traveler or the card on file. Use review_policy when the case facts say
no policy covers the request.
note is at most 60 words: what happened, what the customer asked, and
why a person must decide.
The desk shows the amount from the fare system beside your note, so
never write an amount, a price, a currency, or a number with a decimal
point. Never add any other key.
Write the object once, in under 50 words of note, and stop at its
closing brace: no corrections, no second object, no text after it.

content.text: {"itinerary_ref":"LTG-5591340","asks_for":"review_policy","note":"Customer requests a refund for an airport lounge pass bought from a third party, not sold by Lakeshore. No policy covers third-party purchases, so an approver must decide whether any refund or exception is allowed."}
